1 Introduction
This is a template for the dissertate capability.
Advisors and advisees collaborate on the html version of the thesis/dissertation, with graduate–school format available via pdf download (right side–bar).

title: Dissertation
text:
1.1 Literature review
Citations are specified in BibTeX or BibLaTex format and stored within .bib file(s) located within your project directory.
For example, see the work of Allaire et al. (2026) and Knuth (1984)




Allaire, J. J., Charles Teague, Carlos Scheidegger, Yihui Xie, Christophe Dervieux, and Gordon Woodhull. 2026. “Quarto.” https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5960048.


Knuth, Donald E. 1984. “Literate Programming.” Comput. J. 27 (2): 97–111. https://doi.org/10.1093/comjnl/27.2.97.

title: 2  Methods
text:
You use markdown to indicate formatting – the most important formatting elements for your thesis/dissertation are headings. These will be most directly tied to the look of your graduate school formatted document.
You should also familiarize yourself with cross–references – they will help:

reader navigation of your paper
management of tables and figures

Regarding #1, see Section 4.1
Regarding #2, if you properly cross–reference your tables and figures, you will NOT need to do any manual renumbering or sequencing if (when) your advisor asks for a sequence swap.

title: 3  Results
text:
3.1 Pretty Graph
```{r}
#| label: fig-bubble
#| fig-cap: "Bunch 'o bubbles"

library(plotly)

data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")

fig <- plot_ly(data, x = ~Women, y = ~Men, text = ~School, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers',
        marker = list(size = ~Gap, opacity = 0.5))
fig <- fig %>% layout(title = 'Gender Gap in Earnings per University',
         xaxis = list(showgrid = FALSE),
         yaxis = list(showgrid = FALSE))

fig
```
